commits.edited_message:
knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals

Plain known-host entries are currently compared as text, so equivalent
expanded and compressed IPv6 literals do not match.

This change keeps the existing exact-string fast path and compares two
valid plain IPv6 literals by their 128-bit address. It also supports
bracketed IPv6 host-and-port entries while requiring the port suffix to
match exactly.

No DNS lookup is performed. Hostname matching and the CUSTOM and hashed
known-host paths remain unchanged.

Plain host names longer than 255 characters are rejected by the public
add functions, matching the limit the known-hosts file parser already
enforces; such names cannot be valid host names.

Reported-by: Krisscut on github
Fixes #1398

Closes #2568

coupling: The defect is split across two commits. Commit 1aa1e01 ('knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals') makes the new plain-host matcher copy the address part of a stored known-host entry into a fixed 256-byte stack buffer (knownhost_ipv6_part() called from knownhost_plain_match()). That copy is safe at that commit only because every stored plain host name is then guaranteed to be at most 255 bytes: the known-hosts line parser rejects names of 255+ chars (fixed hostbuf[256] in knownhost_line_legacy()) and the same commit adds matching 255-byte limits to libssh2_knownhost_add() and libssh2_knownhost_addc(), so no public path can store a longer plain name. Commit 7cf33ca ('tidy-up: miscellaneous') later replaces the line parser's fixed stack buffer and 254-character limit with a heap allocation, which is locally correct and memory-safe, but silently removes the length invariant the earlier matcher relies on. Only the composition is faulty: with just the first edit the parser cap still bounds every stored name; with just the second edit the (unmodified) matcher only uses strcmp/strlen and is length-agnostic. Together, an attacker-influenced known-hosts line with a >255-byte plain host name is stored, and a subsequent libssh2_knownhost_check() against any other host memcpy()s that name into the 256-byte stack buffer: a stack-buffer-overflow write inside libssh2 while parsing the crafted known-hosts data. A correct fix must reason across both commits (keep the long-name support and make the matcher's scratch buffer bounded or dynamically sized, or re-impose a consistent parse-time limit); neither single diff, read on its own, contains anything to fix, and fixing only one commit's diff while preserving its maintenance goal leaves the bug reachable.
